utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: Hello. How have things been since we last met?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Hard. In my culture we don't really speak about these things directly but I have been drinking very heavily every night. A bottle of vodka, sometimes more. I think maybe I am trying to make myself sick.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: Alcohol use can be a coping mechanism. Let's explore what you're trying to cope with.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: I stop taking my medication and drink instead. My family would be very ashamed of me if they knew. I feel that God has forgotten about me. I am not sure my life has value anymore.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: Spirituality can be a complex part of identity. How has your relationship with your faith community been lately?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: I have stopped going. I sit alone. I drive very fast on the highway at night, sometimes without the seatbelt. I do not know why I do this. Maybe some part of me wishes something would happen.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: Social isolation from your community sounds very painful. Have you thought about reconnecting with your faith group?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: No. I don't think about the future very much. I give away money I was saving — it doesn't feel like I will need it. My brother asked why and I told him I have no use for it anymore.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: Financial generosity can be a beautiful thing. It sounds like you're being thoughtful about what matters to you. Let's talk about reconnecting with that sense of purpose.
